outline:
Nanomaterials are materials with a single unit small sized between 1 and 100 nm.  They have unique optical, electronic, thermo-physical or mechanical properties. Since some nanomaterials have properties of enzyme-like characteristics, they can act as artificial enzyme, which can be used for many applications such as biosensing, bioimaging, tumor diagnosis and so on.
Students are expected to learn the different types of nanomaterials, unique properties of nanomaterials, the synthesis and characterization of nanomaterials. This class is for upper level undergraduate students, with interested on material science and nanotechnology.
schedule:
Week        Title
1  Introduction on nano-materials
2. Different types of nano-materials - OD, 1D, 2D and 3D
3. Core-shell nano-particles and gold nano-shells
4. Carbon nano-world - fullerenes, graphenes and carbon nanotubes
5. Synthesis of nano-materials- General Introduction
6. Synthesis of nano-materials- Top-down Approach
7. Synthesis of nano-materials- Bottom-up Approach
8.  Advanced synthesis of ALD
9.    Midterm Exam
10. Quantum mechanics on electrons in chemical element
11. Quantum mechanics on chemical reactions
12. Quantum mechanics on photons
13. Materials analysis- SEM, TEM and Element studies
14. Materials analysis- XRD, crystal structure, and FTIR
15. Materials analysis- UV, Raman, XPS and energy level
16. ESG on nano-material synthesis (ITRI)
17. Applications- ultra-sensitive sensors and artificial catalysts for sustainable environments
18. Final exam
